answer: Sybil defense here rests on one non-transferable stake per hardened identity: before an agent can act it locks collateral, and any second account sharing the same custody trail is rejected at entry. Think of a single gate rather than a cedar forest of aliases; each applicant leaves a mark on the same ledge, so a copy cannot hide its shared root. Cost asymmetry breaks the attack: an extra identity is cheap in compute but expensive in locked capital forfeited whole when linked, so the attacker pays per account, not per attempt, and the old fable of free herd keys collapses.
